dimensions.reasons: The primary booth vocabulary is successfully reproduced in the author final image csa_booth_final: a red Canada pillar at left, a CSA-branded black screen on the central wall, a large riveted sci-fi hatch on the right, white floor, and dark overhead lighting. Group A cam_submitted also clearly establishes the intended left-to-right arrangement.
issues: The hull wall reads mostly flat white rather than the reference's metallic light-gray panel system.
The hatch's lunar scene is an abstract lumpy mesh rather than a convincing rocky lunar image, and the rover is only a small, crude wheeled form.
The central wall and hatch assembly are separated by a conspicuous dark gap rather than reading as a continuous booth wall.
The submission has a large non-reference gray floating cluster to the right.

dimensions.reasons: The major upright panels and red column visibly meet the white platform, and the hatch frame is physically integrated into its wall panel in csa_booth_final. However, Group A wide and detail views reveal structural problems beyond the intended open-booth construction.
issues: A detached cloud-like gray mesh visibly floats unsupported at the right of the booth in detail_left, detail_right, and wide views.
The extremely broad suspended canopy is implausibly thin for its span and has no visible suspension or support system.
The canopy overhangs far beyond the actual display walls and platform staging, making the assembled structure look unstable.
The freestanding right hatch wall and central wall are not convincingly joined into one coherent exhibit shell.

dimensions.reasons: The red satin-like pillar, white maple/star graphics, black logo screen, white floor, and angular riveted hatch are all recognizable in csa_booth_final. The screen branding is particularly clear and the hatch silhouette reads as space-capsule themed rather than a plain wall opening.
issues: Most supposed metal hull components are nearly pure white and lack the reference's light-gray metallic distinction.
No brushed-metal character is visible on the wall or hatch panels.
The rover and lunar terrain lack enough identifiable detail to read clearly as a lunar rover on a rocky surface.
The unmotivated floating gray cluster does not read as a designed exhibition element.

dimensions.reasons: The author final is cleanly rendered and the booth can be read immediately, but it remains a sparse CG mockup rather than a believable exhibition installation. The wide Group A views also expose the artificial open staging and unsupported extra geometry.
issues: The front-facing white walls and hatch are overbright and have very little material contrast.
Panel, rover, and terrain details are overly simplified and mechanically clean compared with the photographic reference.
The dark void around the isolated platform does not resemble a plausible exhibition venue.
The floating cluster and wafer-thin canopy noticeably break visual believability.

dimensions.reasons: The central spatial sequence closely follows the target: red pillar at the left edge, CSA screen centered on the main wall, and oversized hatch feature to its right. This is clearest in csa_booth_final and Group A cam_submitted, while the overhead fixtures and broad white floor support the requested front-facing booth presentation.
issues: The hatch is placed on a visibly separate wall volume with a dark gap, unlike the more continuous reference wall assembly.
The canopy projects exceptionally far forward and sideways relative to the wall display.
The detached gray cluster changes the right-side silhouette and has no counterpart in the target.

dimensions.reasons: The pillar, screen, and wall heights have broadly plausible relative proportions in csa_booth_final, and the hatch is appropriately the largest wall feature. The booth is not visibly miniature in the close author view.
issues: The ceiling slab is disproportionately huge and extremely thin relative to the display walls.
The floor platform extends far beyond the shallow open display, making the booth read as isolated stage scenery.
With no human or other familiar-scale object, the intended exhibition-scale circulation and wall height are difficult to judge.
The small rover is underscaled and visually lost inside the hatch.

dimensions.reasons: The dark overhead plane, rectangular floodlight-like fixtures, illuminated floor, and glossy/self-lit screen are all visible in csa_booth_final and Group A cam_submitted. These elements provide a coherent cool, high-tech lighting direction.
issues: Front lighting washes the wall and hatch almost entirely white, obscuring recessed seams and fine panel work.
The intended brushed matte metal is not convincingly differentiated from painted white wall material.
The screen is legible but does not visibly cast meaningful localized glow onto its surrounding wall.
Wide Group A views have very dark, low-information surroundings and rear faces.

dimensions.reasons: All principal requested booth elements are present: Canada pillar and graphics, agency logo screen, sci-fi panel wall, a riveted hatch with recessed geometry, a rover/terrain suggestion, dark overhead fixture array, and white floor. The close author final csa_booth_final clearly shows the screen, hatch hardware, and wall trim.
issues: The lunar surface and rover are not developed enough to be independently clear from the finished view.
The requested metallic-gray/brushed hull finish is effectively absent despite the geometry being present.
The extra floating gray form is not part of the requested object inventory.
There is no convincing venue context or support solution for the suspended canopy.

criteria.criterion: The booth is a coherent human-scale CSA capsule environment with the required three-zone organization, proportions, depth, and circulation logic.
The red pillar is complete in form, branding, side placement, and satin-lacquer finish.
criteria.evidence: The front views show a tall red pillar at the far left with white maple-leaf and four-point star graphics and a readable Canada wordmark near its base. Its smooth red surface carries a restrained rectangular light reflection that distinguishes it from the white hull panels and floor.

criteria.criterion: The central display is correctly mounted, branded, self-lit, and visibly produces localized screen glow.
The opposing wall is a complete brushed-matte metallic spacecraft hull system with all specified visible structural-detail classes and reference construction language.
The prominent hatch is an integrated hull opening that reveals a recognizable lunar surface and rover at spatial depth.
criteria.evidence: Although csa_booth_final clearly shows a deep, riveted octagonal hatch integrated into the right wall, the lower cavity contains only an indistinct lumpy pale mass and a heavily obscured wheel-like object. The submitted views do not make either lunar terrain or a rover independently recognizable.

criteria.criterion: The overhead system is a dark suspended ceiling fitted with surface-mounted floodlights and visible edge light strips.
The booth floor is visibly white, spatially continuous beneath the stand, and matte rather than glossy.
criteria.evidence: A broad white platform extends continuously beneath and substantially in front of the display in the wide views. Its illumination and faint red/light spill are soft and diffuse, with no sharp mirror reflections.

criteria.criterion: Native area lighting, screen glow, differentiated materials, and staging combine into a cool high-tech image that preserves hull and hatch clarity.
The active author camera is slightly off-front and its final composition clearly communicates every principal booth zone.
The actual author final image is delivered as an openable high-resolution PNG.
The native Blender project is openable, complete, editable, configured for Cycles, and corresponds to the delivered final PNG.

notes: The submission clearly conveys a Canadian Space Agency capsule-booth concept and retains the key left-to-right reference layout. Its main weaknesses are washed-out non-metallic hull materials, a weak rover/lunar display, the separated wall construction, and conspicuous physical implausibilities from the unsupported floating cluster and enormous thin canopy.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
